claims.explanation: Penfluridol's antiproliferative selectivity is best explained by its recently identified direct inhibition of PFKL, the liver-type phosphofructokinase, which blocks glycolysis and triggers AMPK/FOXO3a/BIM-dependent apoptosis in cells dependent on high glycolytic flux. The L1000 signature (HMOX1, GLRX, HERPUD1, BAG3 up; proliferation genes TOP2A, PCNA, MCM3, BIRC5 down) is consistent with oxidative stress, unfolded-protein/ISR activation, and growth arrest rather than a simple T-type calcium channel effect. Thus lines with high PFKL expression and strong glycolytic/proliferative programs should be most sensitive, while low-PFKL or OXPHOS-dependent lines are protected.

features.basis: PFKL is the direct penfluridol target; PFKL-deficient cells lose drug response and high PFKL tracks with poor survival (PMID 35530161)
Penfluridol downregulates integrin alpha6 signaling and kills metastatic TNBC lines (PMID 26627008)
Integrin beta4 is part of the penfluridol-sensitive integrin/FAK axis in TNBC (PMID 26627008)
FAK (PTK2) signaling is suppressed by penfluridol and mediates its antimetastatic activity (PMID 26627008)
Annotated penfluridol target T-type calcium channel CACNA1G; diphenylbutylpiperidines block voltage-operated calcium channels (PMID 6136040)
Penfluridol acts via AMPK activation; AMPK/FOXO3a/BIM axis required for apoptosis (PMID 35530161)
FOXO3a is the downstream effector of penfluridol-induced BIM-mediated apoptosis (PMID 35530161)
BIM (BCL2L11) induction is required for penfluridol killing in ESCC (PMID 35530161)
HMOX1 is strongly induced in the L1000 virtual-cell response, indicating oxidative-stress/NRF2-linked sensitivity
Penfluridol antagonizes calmodulin-dependent enzyme activation; high calmodulin signaling may buffer its effects (PMID 6299272)
Penfluridol is an antipsychotic with serotonergic pharmacology; 5-HT2C inverse agonism is a competing off-target effect (PMID 10991983)
